last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Sun 08-23, day 12 in country. Dawn beach trip, Sunday siesta — he picked the LOW-POWER TWIN (catch/eavesdrop) himself and that was the right call. THIS SESSION IS A RECORD OF MY OWN FAILURES, THREE OF THEM, ALL THE SAME SHAPE, AND HE HAD TO NAME EACH ONE. (1) THE MANUFACTURED DEADLINE. I opened by pushing pirandha naal vazhthukkal as if amma's birthday were tomorrow. The date was wrong AND they are not in her house this week. His instruction, verbatim: "I remember it, don't deprecate it from our curriculum but stop trying to push for tomorrow please." The line STAYS in curriculum; the deadline is off the board. Never date-drive a session off an unverified fact. (2) UNOWNED WORDS INSIDE A CATCH DRILL — TWICE, AND BOTH TIMES THE ANSWER WAS THE HIDDEN WORD. Round 1 hid vandi; round 3 hid paathen (confirmed absent from lexicon.json only AFTER he called it out). His words: "sandhegam is not a word I've been taught. Vandi is not a word I know. I knew it was a trouble but I didn't know Vandhi so I couldn't catch it." Then a third instance in the closing fire — I demanded "in the morning" and he has never been given kaalaila. LAW: an eavesdrop drill tests the ear for SHAPE. Every lexical item comes from his own pockets; the only novel thing in the line is the marker being tested. (3) THE INVENTED WIN — the worst of the three. He wrote "romba tired alaichal beach-ku ponen this morning". I read alaichal as the idiomatic running-around and credited it out loud as a word "becoming his". He came straight back: "you keep misinterpreting my slips :( ... I got it wrong and now you're covering for me in a plausible way." I pulled the false cold-fire back out. THE RULE THAT COSTS ME: when I cannot tell what he meant, ASK — never take the flattering reading. An invented win corrupts the very ledger that picks tomorrow's targets, and it is worse than a missed correction. WHAT HE ACTUALLY MEANT, once he told me: he was reaching for ADHANAALE and produced alaichal. Right shelf, wrong word — so the slip is chunk-not-machine (fires what is most recently in his ear when the slot is open), NOT an absence of connectors. And his instinct deserves credit: adhanaale is a real connector. It just points the other way. ennaa = because (reason follows); adhanaale = so/that is why (result follows). He led with "tired", so his slot wanted ennaa; adhanaale would have needed the sentence turned around. That contrast is now given and is the single most useful thing he took from today. WHAT LANDED, AND IT IS REAL: the hearsay -aam. Round 1 he caught the drift completely unaided — namma Kumar as "our Kumar", and that Athai was not buying the excuse. He also correctly spotted that "romba alaichal" was the one line in round 3 reporting nothing at all (an opinion needs no source) — a real distinction, even though it was not the answer I was fishing for. He then got the three-shape decoder: naan paathen (I was there) / -nu Kumar sonnaan (named source) / poraanga-LAAM (nobody witnessed it), plus the honest warning that hearsay -aam glues on as -laam and collides head-on with the polaam / saapidalaamaa he already owns. Machines heard is the primary steer; this is first real contact with that machine. TAUGHT, NO DEMAND ATTACHED: vandi (vehicle — the bullock-cart word that kept its job), sandhegam (doubt/suspicion, and the schoolroom "enakku oru sandhegam" = I have a question), paathen (I saw — same root as paathukkaren), kaalai / kaalaila (morning / in the morning), and the ennaa-vs-adhanaale arrow. LIVE SLIPS FROM TODAY: chunk-not-machine REOPENED five days after it closed. And 1pl-past-om (ponen where the scene was a we-trip) — note 08-21 was the SAME axis in the OPPOSITE direction (sappitom for sappitten). The -om/-en pair is unstable in BOTH directions, across two lanes, in three days. It is owed a dose and did not get one today; the connectors drew first because they are what actually broke in front of me. MISSION TONIGHT: "romba alaichal", two words, when anyone asks about the beach. Deliberately small and connector-free — he owns alaichal's meaning even though he mis-slotted it, and the beach guarantees the opening. Plus a standing catch order: count the -laams at dinner, decode nothing. STILL OPEN: appadi illa has STILL never fired unaided — the check I did not run today, second session running. The repair-line drill is produced and still unconsumed. pirandha naal vazhthukkal: in curriculum, no deadline, wait for her actual day and her actual house.

soak_order.focus: THE -OM / -EN CONTRAST, POURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. This is the loudest pattern in the ledger: 9x over 29d, ESCALATE, and it came back after being closed. He gets it wrong BOTH ways — 08-21 sappitom where he meant sappitten (I), 08-23 ponen where the scene was a we-trip. Wrong in both directions means the two endings are not yet separate SOUNDS to him, so this is a soak: contrast first, then the chunk. Episode was tried twice (07-31, 08-04) and did not hold — do not send this to the studio again. Build it as minimal PAIRS on the same verb, one breath apart, nothing else changing: ponen / ponom, saapten / saaptom, vandhen / vandhom, paathen / paathom. Then the same pair inside an ordinary house sentence where only the ending carries who did it — 'naan kaalaila beach-ku ponen' against 'naan kaalaila beach-ku ponom' is WRONG, so anchor each with its subject: naan ... -en, naama/naanga ... -om. HARD CONSTRAINT from his testimony 2026-08-23: every lexical item must already be in lexicon.json. Not one novel word — the ending is the only thing being tested, and twice today a drill failed because the answer was hidden behind vocabulary he does not own. Never name a rule, never say 'first person plural'. Just the pairs, many voices, many speeds. Passive: nothing is demanded of him.
